title: Encore - Tasty words, colorful sounds - How people with synesthesia experience the world, with Julia Simner, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a summer break, so we're rerunning one of our favorite episodes from the paSt.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》正在进行夏日休整，所以今天我们重播一期过去广受喜爱的节目。

sentences.en: In July 2021, I talked to psychologist Julia Simner about how people with synesthesia experience the world and what we can learn from studying this fascinating condition.
sentences.zh: 在2021年7月，我采访了心理学家朱莉娅·西姆纳，探讨了联觉者是如何体验世界的，以及我们可以从研究这种迷人的现象中学到什么。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back with new episodes in a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 说到《心理学话你知》，我们将在几周后带着新节目回归。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: Words that taste like orange candy.
sentences.zh: 吃起来像橙子糖的文字。

sentences.en: Music that projects brilliant, shimmering colors.
sentences.zh: 能投射出绚丽、闪烁色彩的音乐。

sentences.en: Numbers that come with personalities and full-life stories.
sentences.zh: 带有独特个性和完整人生故事的数字。

sentences.en: These are all forms of synesthesia, a neurological condition in which senses such as taste, touch, smell, and vision link or merge.
sentences.zh: 这些都是联觉的形式，联觉是一种神经系统疾病，味觉、触觉、嗅觉和视觉等感官会在此期间发生连接或融合。

sentences.en: Historical accounts of people with synesthesia date back hundreds of years,
sentences.zh: 关于联觉者的历史记载可以追溯到数百年前，

sentences.en: But it's only in recent decades that scientists have been able to use brain imaging and other modern research methods
sentences.zh: 但直到最近几十年，科学家们才能够利用脑成像和其他现代研究方法

sentences.en: to gain a better understanding of how synesthesia works and why it might occur.
sentences.zh: 来更好地理解联觉是如何运作的以及它为什么会发生。

sentences.en: So what is it like to have synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 那么，拥有联觉是一种什么样的体验？

sentences.en: What might cause it?
sentences.zh: 是什么原因导致了它？

sentences.en: And how do the brains of people with synesthesia differ from those of people without it?
sentences.zh: 为什么联觉者的大脑与非联觉者的大脑有所不同？

sentences.en: What can we learn about the human mind more generally from studying synesthesia and other sensory differences?
sentences.zh: 通过研究联觉和其他感官差异，我们可以对人类思维有怎样更广泛的认识？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Jules Simner, a professor of neuropsychology at the University of Sussex in the United Kingdom, who specializes in multisensory research.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是英国萨塞克斯大学神经心理学教授朱尔斯·西姆纳博士，她专门从事多感官研究。

sentences.en: She has studied synesthesia in adults and children for nearly two decades.
sentences.zh: 她研究成人和儿童的联觉已有近二十年之久。

sentences.en: She also researches other sensory differences, including misophonia, an extreme aversion to certain sounds, and aphantasia, the inability to see pictures in your mind's eye.
sentences.zh: 她还研究其他感官差异，包括恐音症（对某些声音极端厌恶）和失象症（无法在脑海中想象出画面）。

sentences.en: We'll discuss these today, too, and talk about what links these threads of research together.
sentences.zh: 我们今天也会讨论这些话题，并探讨将这些研究线索串联在一起的纽带是什么。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Simner.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能来到节目中，西姆纳博士。

sentences.en: Thanks very much for the invitation.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: Some of our listeners have probably heard of synesthesia, or at least the most common forms of it, like people seeing colors when they hear music.
sentences.zh: 我们的听众可能听说过联觉，或者至少听说过其中最常见的形式，比如人们在听到音乐时会看到颜色。

sentences.en: But synesthesia is a lot more varied than people may realize.
sentences.zh: 但联觉的种类远比人们想象的要丰富得多。

sentences.en: And you've written and tested for 128 different types.
sentences.zh: 您曾经撰文并测试过128种不同的类型。

sentences.en: What types are out there?
sentences.zh: 都有哪些类型呢？

sentences.en: What are the differences and the commonalities?
sentences.zh: 它们的区别和共同点是什么？

sentences.en: So it's quite hard to estimate exactly how many types of synesthesia there are, because some could be quite well hidden.
sentences.zh: 所以很难准确估计究竟有多少种联觉，因为有些可能隐藏得很好。

sentences.en: But the ones we know most about are the ones that people can realize most readily and report to us most easily.
sentences.zh: 但我们了解最多的，是那些人们最容易察觉并最容易向我们报告的类型。

sentences.en: And I think for that reason, we tend to think of the most common types of synesthesia as being the ones that trigger unusual color perceptions.
sentences.zh: 我想正因如此，我们往往认为最常见的联觉类型是那些会触发异常颜色感知的类型。

sentences.en: So experiencing colors when you are reading words, looking at numbers, listening to music, and then perhaps more obscurely swimming.
sentences.zh: 比如你在阅读文字、看数字、听音乐时体验到颜色，然后或许更晦涩一点的是游泳。

sentences.en: So different swimming strokes causing different color perceptions.
sentences.zh: 不同的泳姿会引起不同的色彩感知。

sentences.en: Perhaps even reading Braille also and watching signers in sign language.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能包括阅读盲文以及观看手语中的手语者。

sentences.en: All of these are known to trigger colors.
sentences.zh: 已知所有这些都会引发颜色。

sentences.en: But as I said, although people talk about colors most often in the context of synesthesia, I think it may be that colors are just the easiest to report,
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，尽管人们在联觉的语境下最常谈论颜色，但我认为这可能是因为颜色最容易被报告出来，

sentences.en: because there are many different other synesthetic sensations.
sentences.zh: 因为还有许多其他不同的联觉感觉。

sentences.en: So you could experience flavors that flood the mouth.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以体验到充满口腔的风味。

sentences.en: So you're reading and your mouth is being bombarded with sensations of Yorkshire pudding or processed peas or bitter lemon or nice orange fruit sweets,
sentences.zh: 你在阅读时，口腔会被约克郡布丁、加工青豆、苦柠檬或好吃的橙味水果糖等感觉狂轰滥炸，

sentences.en: which is what Julia tastes of, my name, Julia, or perhaps less pleasant taste.
sentences.zh: 这也是我的名字朱莉娅（Julia）所尝到的味道，或者也许是不那么愉悦的味道。

sentences.en: So the taste of earwax or other things that you wouldn't want in your mouth, maybe vomit and so on.
sentences.zh: 比如耳屎的味道，或者其他你不想放进嘴里的东西，比如呕吐物等等。

sentences.en: So that's also another type of synesthesia we know about.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是我们所知的另一种联觉。

sentences.en: But to answer your question, there are many different kinds of synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 但回答你的问题，联觉有很多不同的种类。

sentences.en: They can trigger colors, tastes, smells, textures, bodily feelings, and the compulsion even to put your body into certain shapes or formations.
sentences.zh: 它们可以触发颜色、味道、气味、质感、身体感觉，甚至会产生一种强迫感，让你把身体摆成特定的形状或姿势。

sentences.en: So I remember a very rare case from many years ago of a professor who had an urge to form shapes with his body in response to different words that he heard.
sentences.zh: 我记得多年前一个非常罕见的案例，有一位教授，当他听到不同的词语时，会产生一种用身体摆出各种形状的冲动。

sentences.en: So many types.
sentences.zh: 所以种类非常多。

sentences.en: So you said your name has a flavor.
sentences.zh: 您刚才说您的名字有一种味道。

sentences.en: Is that universal?
sentences.zh: 这是普遍存在的吗？

sentences.en: How does your name have a flavor?
sentences.zh: 您的名字怎么会有味道呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: So what I described to you, and I think he wouldn't mind me mentioning this at all,
sentences.zh: 我向你描述的，我想他不会介意我提起这件事，

sentences.en: what I described to you was the taste of the name Julia as experienced by synesthete James Wannerton.
sentences.zh: 我向你描述的是联觉者詹姆斯·旺纳顿（James Wannerton）所体验到的名字朱莉娅的味道。

sentences.en: Now, James Wannerton is a particularly special and important synesthete for me.
sentences.zh: 现在，詹姆斯·旺纳顿对我来说是一个非常特别且重要的联觉者。

sentences.en: Not only have I studied James for the last 20 years, but James has been an amazing advocate for the synesthesia community.
sentences.zh: 不仅因为我在过去20年里一直在研究詹姆斯，而且詹姆斯一直是联觉社群的非凡倡导者。

sentences.en: He is the president of the UK Synesthesia Association, and he has taken part in so much outreach himself to help people to understand the condition.
sentences.zh: 他是英国联觉协会的主席，并且亲自参与了大量的推广活动，以帮助人们了解这种状况。

sentences.en: And for James, the name Julia tastes of orange fruit sweets.
sentences.zh: 对詹姆斯而言，“朱莉娅”这个名字尝起来像橙味水果糖。

sentences.en: It's actually a branded fruit sweet.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一种有品牌的果糖。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing is most people call me Jules Simner.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，大多数人叫我朱尔斯·西姆纳（Jules Simner）。

sentences.en: They use my nickname Jules.
sentences.zh: 他们用我的昵称朱尔斯（Jules）。

sentences.en: But with James, we don't do that because Jules does not taste as nice as Julia.
sentences.zh: 但在詹姆斯这里，我们不用这个称呼，因为朱尔斯尝起来没有朱莉娅那么好。

sentences.en: Jules has a bit of an unpleasant taste.
sentences.zh: 朱尔斯有一种稍微不太愉悦的味道。

sentences.en: James politely tells me it tastes of porridge.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯礼貌地告诉我，它尝起来像粥。

sentences.en: I think it may actually taste of drool or saliva because we know that there are links between the word that triggers synesthesia and the type of taste experienced.
sentences.zh: 我想它实际上可能尝起来像口水或唾液，因为我们知道，触发联觉的词语与所体验到的味道类型之间存在着某种联系。

sentences.en: And from my 20 years of research, I rather suspect that Jules tastes of drool, which is why we use the name Julia.
sentences.zh: 根据我20年的研究，我相当怀疑朱尔斯尝起来像口水，这就是为什么我们用朱莉娅这个名字。

sentences.en: So do people with music and color synesthesia actually see colors in the world around them when they hear music?
sentences.zh: 那么，拥有音乐和颜色联觉的人在听到音乐时，真的会在他们周围的世界中看到颜色吗？

sentences.en: Or is it more like just something in their mind's eye?
sentences.zh: 还是更像是他们脑海中的某种想象？

sentences.en: So the answer to that depends on the synesthete you're speaking to, because there are several different ways that synesthetes can experience their color.
sentences.zh: 所以这个问题的答案取决于你所交谈的联觉者，因为联觉者体验颜色的方式有几种不同的途径。

sentences.en: So this was captured quite nicely by our colleagues, Mike Dixon and Daniel Smillik and their team in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我们的加拿大同事迈克·迪克森（Mike Dixon）和丹尼尔·斯米利克（Daniel Smilek）及其团队很好地捕捉到了这一点。

sentences.en: They were able to name projector synesthetes versus associator synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 他们将其命名为投射型联觉者与联想型联觉者。

sentences.en: So associator synesthetes experience their colors somewhere in the mind's eye, like a kind of strong internal mental imagery.
sentences.zh: 联想型联觉者在脑海中的某个地方体验他们的颜色，就像一种强烈内部心理意象。

sentences.en: Projector synesthetes will see their colors projected out in the outside world.
sentences.zh: 投射型联觉者会看到他们的颜色被投射到外部世界中。

sentences.en: So a couple of examples.
sentences.zh: 举几个例子。

sentences.en: If you have colored letters and numbers and are a projector synesthetes, you may see those colors superimposed onto the text that you're reading.
sentences.zh: 如果你有带颜色的字母和数字，并且是一名投射型联觉者，你可能会看到这些颜色叠加在你正在阅读的文本上。

sentences.en: Or if I'm sure he wouldn't mind me describing, or as described to me by synesthesia scientist Julian Asher, those colors can be projected out there in the world floating in space.
sentences.zh: 或者——我相信他不会介意我这样描述，正如联觉科学家朱利安·阿舍（Julian Asher）向我描述的那样——这些颜色可以被投射到现实世界中，漂浮在太空中。

sentences.en: So Julian Asher is a geneticist who helped us to understand the genetics of synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 朱利安·阿舍是一位遗传学家，他帮助我们理解了联觉的遗传学机制。

sentences.en: And he told me that when he was a young boy, his parents would take him to the symphony.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，当他还是个小男孩的时候，他的父母会带他去听交响乐。

sentences.en: And he assumed that the house lights dimmed so that people could see the colors better.
sentences.zh: 他以为剧场的灯光变暗是为了让人能更好地看到颜色。

sentences.en: Because for him, the orchestra has colors floating above it.
sentences.zh: 因为对他来说，管弦乐队上方漂浮着各种颜色。

sentences.en: And he actually thought, why else would anybody dim the house lights, apart from to see the synesthetic colors better?
sentences.zh: 他甚至想，除了为了更好地看到联觉的颜色之外，还有谁会把剧场灯光调暗呢？

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: So in your mind, or in the outside world, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以是在你的脑海里，或者是在外部世界，是的。

sentences.en: And sometimes experienced in unusual ways.
sentences.zh: 有时会以不寻常的方式体验到。

sentences.en: I remember a student of mine from 20 years ago who experienced pain as colors.
sentences.zh: 我记得20年前我有一个学生，她将疼痛体验为颜色。

sentences.en: And for her, the colors were a cone that projected from her head in color.
sentences.zh: 对她而言，这些颜色是从她头部投射出的一个彩色圆锥体。

sentences.en: And if she thought very hard about the shape of the cone, she could moderate the pain of the headache.
sentences.zh: 如果她努力去思考这个圆锥体的形状，她就能减轻头痛带来的痛苦。

sentences.en: How common is synesthesia and what's the prevalence in the population?
sentences.zh: 联觉有多普遍？它在人群中的患病率是多少？

sentences.en: Do we know?
sentences.zh: 我们知道吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，知道。

sentences.en: So this is something I've spent quite a lot of the last 20 years looking into.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在过去20年里花了很多时间去研究的课题。

sentences.en: Our first estimates for commonness were based on asking synesthetes to come forward.
sentences.zh: 我们对普遍性的最初估计是基于号召联觉者主动前来。

sentences.en: So there was a very nice study by Simon Baron-Cohen and his colleagues in 1996.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·巴伦-科恩（Simon Baron-Cohen）及其同事在1996年做过一项非常棒的研究。

sentences.en: And they placed an advert in the newspaper in Cambridge, UK.
sentences.zh: 他们在英国剑桥的一家报纸上刊登了一则广告。

sentences.en: And it described synesthesia and it asked synesthetes to come forward.
sentences.zh: 广告描述了联觉并呼吁联觉者站出来。

sentences.en: And he found that the prevalence of synesthesia was 1 in 2000 from that study.
sentences.zh: 通过那项研究，他发现联觉的患病率是两千分之一。

sentences.en: Now, of course, unfortunately, and of course they knew this, they would be radically underestimating because they were relying on synesthetes to buy the newspaper that day,
sentences.zh: 当然，不幸的是，而且他们也知道这一点，他们严重低估了这一数字，因为他们依赖于联觉者在那天购买报纸、

sentences.en: to read the article, to come forward, you know, which are lots of things that filter out people through that process.
sentences.zh: 阅读文章并站出来，你知道的，这个过程会通过很多环节筛选掉一部分人。

sentences.en: So in 2000 and in the early 2000s, my colleague Jamie Ward and I decided to, instead of relying on synesthetes to come forward, we started to go out into the general population.
sentences.zh: 所以在2000年以及2000年代初，我的同事杰米·沃德（Jamie Ward）和我决定，不再依赖联觉者主动站出来，而是走向广大普通人群。

sentences.en: We would gather large groups of people together and screen every single one of them.
sentences.zh: 我们会把大量的人聚集在一起，对每一个人进行筛查。

sentences.en: And this gave us a sort of better estimate, really, of the prevalence of synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 这确实让我们对联觉的患病率有了更好的估计。

sentences.en: And since then, I've individually screened almost 20,000 people for synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我亲自为近两万人筛查了联觉。

sentences.en: And from that, we have quite a good idea that synesthesia is at least 4.4% in the population.
sentences.zh: 由此，我们对联觉在人群中的比例有了相当不错的了解，至少为4.4%。

sentences.en: So at least 1 in 23 people have synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，至少每23个人中就有1个人患有联觉。

sentences.en: In that study, we were looking at around 140 different types of synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 在那项研究中，我们研究了大约140种不同的联觉类型。

sentences.en: But we had missed out some quite crucial types.
sentences.zh: 但我们也漏掉了一些非常关键的类型。

sentences.en: So we also know independently that around 10% of people see time or numbers or letters mapped out in space.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们通过独立研究得知，大约10%的人在空间中映射时间、数字或字母。

sentences.en: Now, that would add another sort of 10% to that figure that I gave earlier.
sentences.zh: 这会在我刚才给出的数字上再加上大约10%。

sentences.en: We also know that at least 1% to 2% of the population have personalities for letters, numbers, days of the week, months of the year.
sentences.zh: 我们还知道，至少有1%到2%的人对字母、数字、星期、月份拥有性格特征感。

sentences.en: So we would have to add that on as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还得把这个也加上。

sentences.en: But it does really come down to what you think synesthesia is.
sentences.zh: 但这其实取决于你认为什么是联觉。

sentences.en: If you think these numbers are getting quite high, they are.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这些数字变得相当高，确实如此。

sentences.en: But you might want to question whether numbers mapped out in space, whether time mapped out in space, is a synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会质疑，空间中映射的数字、空间中映射的时间到底算不算联觉。

sentences.en: Because 10% of the population experiencing that makes us start to question, well, is this really synesthesia at all?
sentences.zh: 因为有10%的人口体验到这一点，这让我们开始质疑，这真的是联觉吗？

sentences.en: But a very simple answer is at least 4% of the population.
sentences.zh: 但一个非常简单的答案是，至少4%的人口拥有联觉。

sentences.en: Now, that's an interesting prevalence because that feels small.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的患病率，因为这听起来比例很小。

sentences.en: 4.4% feels small, but it's actually equivalent to the entire population of the United States in the world.
sentences.zh: 4.4%听起来很少，但它实际上相当于世界上整个美国人口的规模。

sentences.en: So if you were to gather all synesthetes together, that would be 307 million synesthetes worldwide, which is, you know, somewhere approximating the USA population.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你把所有的联觉者聚集在一起，全球将有3.07亿联觉者，你知道的，这大致相当于美国的总人口。

sentences.en: So it's a rare condition, but not insignificant.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种罕见的病症，但并不微不足道。

sentences.en: And do you know, is it more common in men or women, or is it equally distributed?
sentences.zh: 你知道它在男性中更常见还是在女性中更常见，还是男女分布均匀？

sentences.en: See, that's a very nice question, again, because it speaks to methodologies.
sentences.zh: 看，这又是一个非常好的问题，因为它触及了方法论。

sentences.en: So this early study of prevalence conducted by placing an advert in the newspaper and asking synesthetes to come forward,
sentences.zh: 通过在报纸上登广告并号召联觉者主动现身来进行的早期患病率研究，

sentences.en: gave the very, very strong impression that it was a female trait.
sentences.zh: 给人留下了非常深刻的印象，即它是一种女性特征。

sentences.en: Because I think something like eight times as many female synesthetes were found as males.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得发现的女性联觉者数量大约是男性的八倍。

sentences.en: So it put across the message that synesthesia was a female trait, and that stayed with us for about a decade.
sentences.zh: 因此它传递出的信息是，联觉是一种女性特质，这种观念伴随了我们大约十年。

sentences.en: However, it turns out that that was a trick of the methodology, a confound in the methodology.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实证明这只是方法论上的一个小把戏，是方法论中的一个混杂因素。

sentences.en: Because in fact, we know from many other studies that women with unusual conditions are simply more likely to come forward.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，我们从许多其他研究中得知，患有不常见病症的女性只是更愿意主动站出来。

sentences.en: So what we actually have is a condition which is balanced across the senses.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上面对的是一种在各性别间均衡分布的状况。

sentences.en: When you go out and screen people through a large population, you find the same number of male and female synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 当你走出去对大量人群进行筛查时，你会发现数量相当的男女联觉者。

sentences.en: But when you ask them to come forward, the men hold back and the women reach out to scientists.
sentences.zh: 但当你要求他们主动前来时，男性选择退缩，而女性则向科学家伸出了援手。

sentences.en: You know, I mentioned in the introduction that in the past couple of decades,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我在引言中提到过，在过去的几十年里，

sentences.en: scientists have begun using brain scans to understand what's happening in the brains of people with synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 科学家们开始使用脑部扫描来了解联觉者的大脑中究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: What have they found?
sentences.zh: 他们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Do the brains of people with synesthesia look different or function differently from the brains of people who don't have it?
sentences.zh: 联觉者的大脑与没有联觉的人的大脑看起来不同，或者功能运作不同吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think brain imaging in synesthesia has been the most important scientific step forward in 200 years.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为联觉的脑成像研究是200年来最伟大的科学飞跃。

sentences.en: I remember giving synesthesia lectures and synesthesia talks before the advent of these brain imaging findings.
sentences.zh: 我记得在这些脑成像发现问世之前，我做过关于联觉的演讲和讲座。

sentences.en: And I would spend the entire talk trying to persuade people that synesthesia was real.
sentences.zh: 那时我会花整场演讲的时间试图说服人们联觉是真实存在的。

sentences.en: Now, somewhere around 2005, we got a sudden proliferation of imaging studies.
sentences.zh: 现在，大约在2005年前后，我们迎来了成像研究的突然爆发。

sentences.en: And that was wonderful because now when I give synesthesia talks, the first thing I do is show the brain of a synesthete in an fMRI image, for example, and the brain of a control.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了，因为现在当我做关于联觉的演讲时，我做的第一件事就是在fMRI（功能性磁共振成像）图像中展示联觉者的大脑和对照组的大脑。

sentences.en: And they're so very different that I no longer have to struggle to persuade people on genuineness.
sentences.zh: 它们差异如此之大，以至于我再也不用费力去说服别人它的真实性了。

sentences.en: So what do they show?
sentences.zh: 那么它们显示了什么？

sentences.en: So these brain imaging studies show very nicely that the brains of synesthetes are different to those of people without synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 这些脑成像研究非常漂亮地表明，联觉者的大脑与没有联觉的人的大脑是不同的。

sentences.en: They're different in their functionality.
sentences.zh: 它们在功能上有所不同。

sentences.en: So in fMRI,
sentences.zh: 在fMRI中，

sentences.en: we can see that color selective regions or regions close to color areas in the visual cortex will light up in response to reading black and white numbers for synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到，当联觉者阅读黑白数字时，视觉皮层中的颜色选择性区域或靠近颜色区域的区域会被激活。

sentences.en: When obviously for controls, those same regions would only light up if they were exposed to color in the real world.
sentences.zh: 而对对照组来说，显而易见，只有当他们在现实世界中接触到颜色时，这些相同的区域才会亮起。

sentences.en: And also some very nice data from our Dutch colleagues has shown that synesthetes have different structural qualities in their brain.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们荷兰同事的一些非常棒的数据表明，联觉者大脑中存在不同的结构特征。

sentences.en: So differences in their white matter coherence in different parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 即大脑不同部位白质连贯性的差异。

sentences.en: So greater white matter connectivity, near color selective regions, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，颜色选择性区域附近的白质连接性更强。

sentences.en: Also, other interesting differences, differences in frontal areas, differences in parietal areas that might be linked to a greater binding.
sentences.zh: 还有其他有趣的差异，比如额叶区域的差异、顶叶区域的差异，这些可能与更强大的绑定能力有关。

sentences.en: So binding is where we bring together different features of the world.
sentences.zh: 绑定就是我们将世界的不同特征组合在一起的过程。

sentences.en: So, for example, if I look at a green apple, the greenness is in one part of my brain, the shape of the apple is in another part of my brain.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果我看着一个青苹果，绿色的属性在我大脑的一部分，苹果的形状在我大脑的另一部分。

sentences.en: The binding region helps to bring those pieces of information together.
sentences.zh: 结合区域有助于将这些信息片段整合在一起。

sentences.en: And synesthetes have differences in parietal areas that deal with binding, almost as if they're overbinding features.
sentences.zh: 联觉者的顶叶区域在处理结合时存在差异，几乎就像他们在过度结合特征一样。

sentences.en: They're not only binding the colors of apples to the shapes of apples, they're binding the colors of apples to letters and numbers and music and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅将苹果的颜色与苹果的形状结合起来，还将苹果的颜色与字母、数字、音乐等结合起来。

sentences.en: So, yeah, brain imaging has really revolutionized what you do.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，脑成像确实彻底改变了你们的研究工作。

sentences.en: So do researchers like you have any theories as to why synesthesia develops?
sentences.zh: 那么像您这样的研究人员对于联觉是如何产生的有什么理论吗？

sentences.en: And is it hereditary?
sentences.zh: 它会遗传吗？

sentences.en: Is there a cause or are you just born with it?
sentences.zh: 是有某个成因，还是天生就有的？

sentences.en: So on the question of inheritance, it does seem to be genetically endowed in some way rather than, well, for a start, we do know, first of all,
sentences.zh: 关于遗传的问题，它在某种程度上似乎是天生基因赋予的，而不是……好吧，首先，我们确实知道，最重要的一点是，

sentences.en: that it passes down through families.
sentences.zh: 它是通过家族世代相传的。

sentences.en: So a study back in 2005 with my colleague Jamie Ward showed that if you have synesthesia in the family, you're much more likely to have it sort of,
sentences.zh: 因此，我和同事杰米·沃德（Jamie Ward）在2005年做过一项研究，结果表明，如果你的家族中有人患有联觉，你更有可能会……

sentences.en: you're more likely to have it popping up through generations than much more likely than you expect from chance alone.
sentences.zh: 它在家族代际中出现的几率，远高于你仅凭随机偶然性所预期的几率。

sentences.en: So it's passing through families.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在家族中代代相传的。

sentences.en: Now, of course, it could be learned.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也有可能是后天习得的。

sentences.en: It could be parents teaching children.
sentences.zh: 可能是父母教给孩子的。

sentences.en: But we know that's not the case for several reasons.
sentences.zh: 但由于几个原因，我们知道事实并非如此。

sentences.en: First of all, parents and children are likely to have very different kinds of synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 首先，父母和孩子很可能会拥有截然不同的联觉类型。

sentences.en: So what's being passed on is a sort of predisposition for synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 所以传承下来的其实是一种对联觉的某种倾向性。

sentences.en: But you might have a parent with colored letters whose son has tasty words.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会遇到这样的情况：父母看字母有颜色，而他们的儿子觉得字词有味道。

sentences.en: And so that suggests it's not being taught through the generations.
sentences.zh: 这就表明它并不是通过代际教导传下来的。

sentences.en: And quite often for that reason, families are not aware that they have so much synesthesia going on.
sentences.zh: 也正因如此，往往很多家族并没有意识到他们身上存在着这么多的联觉现象。

sentences.en: So if I'm a person with colored letters, why would I suddenly ask my child what's the taste of Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我是一个觉得字母有颜色的人，我为什么会突然问我的孩子“星期二是什么味道”呢？

sentences.en: It wouldn't happen.
sentences.zh: 这根本不会发生。

sentences.en: So quite often you get these families with multiple variants appearing.
sentences.zh: 因此，你经常会发现这些家族中出现了多种不同的联觉变体。

sentences.en: And then there are more direct genetics findings.
sentences.zh: 然后还有更直接的遗传学发现。

sentences.en: So I mentioned earlier Julian Asher did some pioneering research with Simon Baron Cohen on the genetics.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，朱利安·阿什尔（Julian Asher）曾与西蒙·巴伦-科恩（Simon Baron Cohen）在遗传学方面进行过开创性的研究。

sentences.en: More recently, the Max Planck Institute in Nijmegen has got a fantastic genetics project going on, screening hundreds and hundreds and hundreds,
sentences.zh: 最近，位于奈梅亨的马克斯·普朗克研究所正在进行一项极棒的遗传学项目，他们筛查了成百上千个、

sentences.en: hopefully thousands and thousands of synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 甚至希望能筛查成千上万个联觉者。

sentences.en: And finding hotspots on chromosomes that are suggestive of synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 并找到了染色体上暗示联觉存在的“热点区域”。

sentences.en: It's unfortunately, it's not a clean picture.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，情况并非那么明朗。

sentences.en: Sometimes in the genetics, it's quite easy to point to genes.
sentences.zh: 有时在遗传学中，直接指出相关基因是相当容易的。

sentences.en: What we're finding is that different families seem to have different families and different variants of synesthesia seem to have different genetic profiles.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现的是，不同的家族以及不同类型的联觉变体，似乎拥有不同的基因特征。

sentences.en: So it hasn't been a very easy task or a very clean picture, but we have got these areas on the genome that are hotspots, if you like,
sentences.zh: 所以这项任务并不轻松，情况也远非清晰明了，但我们在基因组上确实找到了这些热点区域，如果你愿意这么叫的话，

sentences.en: for certain kinds of synesthesia in certain families.
sentences.zh: 它们对应着某些家族中的某些特定联觉。

sentences.en: So if a person with synesthesia experiences trauma, such as a blow to the head or even a very high fever, is that something that could make the synesthesia disappear?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果一个患有联觉的人经历了创伤，例如头部受到撞击，甚至是高烧，这种情况会使联觉消失吗？

sentences.en: And conversely, if you didn't have it, but then you experienced a blow to the head, could it trigger synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 相反，如果你本来没有联觉，但后来头部受到了撞击，这会触发联觉吗？

sentences.en: Or is that just an off-the-wall question?
sentences.zh: 还是这只是一个异想天开的问题？

sentences.en: Actually, I think both those things are true.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这两种情况都是真的。

sentences.en: There are rare cases of acquired synesthesia after trauma.
sentences.zh: 创伤后获得性联觉的罕见案例是确实存在的。

sentences.en: There are also cases of synesthesia disappearing under certain circumstances.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，联觉也会消失。

sentences.en: Now, it's not very well studied because obviously we can't replicate this very well in the lab and nor would we want to, because I wouldn't be the person to take away synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 不过，这个领域并没有得到充分研究，因为很显然我们无法在实验室里很好地复制这种情况，我们也不想这么做，因为我可不想成为那个剥夺别人联觉的人。

sentences.en: But there are cases, there's anecdotal reports.
sentences.zh: 但确实有一些案例，也有一些传闻报告。

sentences.en: There's some really reliable anecdotal reports.
sentences.zh: 有一些非常可靠的传闻报告。

sentences.en: So there is a case of a very prominent synesthete who very sadly experienced the Japanese earthquake and felt for some time afterwards that his synesthesia was deadened.
sentences.zh: 曾有一位非常著名的联觉者，他非常不幸地经历了日本大地震，并在之后的很长一段时间里，觉得自己的联觉变得迟钝了。

sentences.en: And that was quite a troubling thing for him to deal with.
sentences.zh: 这对当时的他在心理上是一个不小的困扰。

sentences.en: Luckily, it's come back.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，它又恢复了。

sentences.en: I've had also synesthetes contacting me, asking me about medication.
sentences.zh: 也有联觉者联系过我，向我咨询关于药物的事情。

sentences.en: They're on a medication and suddenly the synesthesia is attenuated.
sentences.zh: 他们正在服某种药物，结果联觉突然减弱了。

sentences.en: When we give large surveys to synesthetes and ask them for self-reports, sometimes reports of caffeine making differences.
sentences.zh: 当我们对联觉者进行大规模调查并要求他们进行自我报告时，有时会听到咖啡因会带来改变的说法。

sentences.en: But it's very hard for us to pin this down in the lab.
sentences.zh: 但要在实验室里把这一点明确证实是非常困难的。

sentences.en: So quite often you'll find these reports in case study journals, which are really useful.
sentences.zh: 因此，你经常会在案例研究期刊中发现这些报告，它们真的非常有用。

sentences.en: So one thing that you've written about that I found surprising was that people are not always reliable reporters of whether they have synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 那么，您曾写过一篇文章，其中提到了一点让我感到意外：人们对于自己是否拥有联觉，并不总是可靠的报告者。

sentences.en: Some people with it don't realize they have it.
sentences.zh: 有些拥有联觉的人并没有意识到自己有。

sentences.en: Some non-synesthetes will say that they do.
sentences.zh: 而有些没有联觉的人却说自己有。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: And how do you test to determine whether someone actually has synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 你们又是如何测试以确定某人是否真的拥有联觉的？

sentences.en: So the first time I came across this, I was really surprised by quite how inaccurate self-report is in synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次遇到这种情况时，我真的很惊讶，联觉的自我报告竟然如此不准确。

sentences.en: Let me answer this by telling you how we verify synesthesia, first of all.
sentences.zh: 首先，让我通过告诉你我们如何验证联觉来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: So we have a very nice test for synesthesia that seems robust and has been used since 1989, early 90s.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个非常棒的联觉测试，它看起来很稳健，自1989年或90年代初以来一直被使用。

sentences.en: Again, this was a very nice test that Simon Baron-Cohen was able to pioneer.
sentences.zh: 这也是西蒙·巴伦-科恩能够开创的一个非常棒的测试。

sentences.en: So we test synesthetes by looking for a trait called consistency over time.
sentences.zh: 我们通过寻找一个被称为“随时间推移的一致性”的特征来测试联觉者。

sentences.en: So what we do is we ask synesthetes to tell us their associations.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是要求联觉者告诉我们他们的联觉对应关系。

sentences.en: And in fact, we do this in more sophisticated ways.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们用更复杂的方法来做到这一点。

sentences.en: So, for example, we have tests that show the letters and numbers in a random order.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们的测试会以随机顺序显示字母和数字。

sentences.en: Every time a grapheme appears, the synesthetes required to choose the specific synesthetic color from a really fine grain color palette that has like 16 million colors.
sentences.zh: 每当一个字素出现时，联觉者被要求从一个非常细腻、拥有约1600万种颜色的调色盘中，选出其特定的联觉颜色。

sentences.en: So an A will appear, the synesthetes will choose their exact shade of red.
sentences.zh: 所以当字母A出现时，联觉者会选出他们那精准的红色色调。

sentences.en: A 7 will appear, the synesthetes will choose their exact shade of green and so on.
sentences.zh: 当数字7出现时，联觉者会选出他们那精准的绿色色调，以此类推。

sentences.en: And once they get to the end of the test, we surprise synesthetes and we repeat it.
sentences.zh: 当他们完成测试的最后一部分时，我们会给联觉者一个惊喜，那就是重复测试。

sentences.en: So they do the whole thing over and over again.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会把整个过程一遍又一遍地做下去。

sentences.en: And they can do this anything from twice to maybe three times.
sentences.zh: 他们可以重复两到三次不等。

sentences.en: And what we have at the end is each letter and number with the colors given to it over time by the same synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 最后我们得到的结果是：同一个联觉者在不同时间给出的每个字母和数字所对应的颜色。

sentences.en: And then we can use a technique that allows us to look at color distances.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们可以使用一种技术来观察颜色的距离。

sentences.en: So when I ask you for the color of A the first time and the second time, I plot those colors in space and I say, how close are they in space?
sentences.zh: 当我第一次和第二次询问你字母A的颜色时，我把这些颜色绘制在空间坐标中，然后我会问：它们在空间中有多接近？

sentences.en: Now, if you are consistent, those colors will be very close in color space.
sentences.zh: 如果你具有一致性，这些颜色在色彩空间中会非常接近。

sentences.en: You'll have said the same shade of red twice.
sentences.zh: 你两次说出的会是同一种红色的色调。

sentences.en: If you ask a control, they'll be inventing it, making it up very inconsistent, very large distances in color space.
sentences.zh: 如果你问的是对照组的普通人，他们会凭空捏造、胡乱编造，非常不一致，在色彩空间中的距离会非常大。

sentences.en: So we can quantify the consistency of a synesthetes in terms of, you know, distances in color space.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以用色彩空间中的距离来量化联觉者的一致性。

sentences.en: And this shows us that synesthetes are very, very, very consistent.
sentences.zh: 这向我们展示了联觉者具有非常非常高的一致性。

sentences.en: You're not going to fool them.
sentences.zh: 你是无法欺骗他们的。

sentences.en: If you say what color is 7, they're always going to tell you exactly the same shade of, I don't know, subtle lime green.
sentences.zh: 如果你问数字7是什么颜色，他们总是会告诉你完全相同的……我不知道，那种微妙的青柠绿的色调。

sentences.en: They're going to be spot on and controls are going to be inconsistent.
sentences.zh: 他们会分毫不差，而对照组的人则会前后不一致。

sentences.en: And so we have a threshold of consistency.
sentences.zh: 所以我们设定了一个一致性阈值。

sentences.en: Synesthetes have to be above the threshold in order to be validated as a synesthete.
sentences.zh: 联觉者必须超过这个阈值，才能被证实为真正的联觉者。

sentences.en: So when we run these tests, we usually start by saying, first of all, this is synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们进行这些测试时，我们通常首先会问：首先，这就是联觉。

sentences.en: Have you got synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 你有联觉吗？

sentences.en: And you would think that everybody who says yes goes on to be consistent and everybody who says no goes on to be inconsistent.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，所有回答“是”的人接下来都会表现出一致性，而所有回答“否”的人接下来都会表现出不一致性。

sentences.en: But actually, what we find is that for every true, consistent synesthete who says they have synesthesia, there are five non-synesthetes saying they have synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们发现：对于每一个说自己有联觉且通过一致性验证的真正联觉者来说，都有五个并没有联觉的人说自己有联觉。

sentences.en: And the reasons are actually not too surprising.
sentences.zh: 原因其实并不难理解。

sentences.en: There's a tiny bit of social desirability.
sentences.zh: 其中有一点点社会期许效应的影响。

sentences.en: It's quite nice to say you have something interesting.
sentences.zh: 说自己有一些有趣的事情是挺讨人喜欢的。

sentences.en: But actually, there are a lot of artists who say they have synesthesia because what they have is a really fine-grained appreciation for color.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，有很多艺术家说自己有联觉，因为他们对颜色有着非常细腻的鉴赏力。

sentences.en: And that's quite easy to confuse.
sentences.zh: 而这很容易被混淆。

sentences.en: So lots of the non-synesthetes reporting synesthesia are artists.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多声称自己有联觉的非联觉者其实都是艺术家。

sentences.en: Some of them are just sort of, some of them are just mistaken.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人只是……有些只是弄错了。

sentences.en: Some of them are just not concentrating.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人只是不够专注。

sentences.en: But all in all, if I ever now review papers on synesthesia where there's no consistency test, it's dead in the water because you don't know you have synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 但总而言之，如果我现在审阅关于联觉的论文时，发现其中没有一致性测试，那这篇论文就毫无价值了，因为你根本不知道受试者是不是真正的联觉者。

sentences.en: So you were talking about artists and creative types.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才谈到了艺术家和富有创造力的人。

sentences.en: Is it more likely that a person who is creative and is an artist would have synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 富有创造力和身为艺术家的人更有可能拥有联觉吗？

sentences.en: Is there actually some association?
sentences.zh: 这两者之间真的有什么关联吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yes, there seems to be.
sentences.zh: 是的，似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: So first of all, if you look within creative disciplines, you're more likely to find synesthetes.
sentences.zh: 首先，如果你在创意领域内部观察，你会发现更多联觉者。

sentences.en: Now, that makes it difficult because artists are more likely to inaccurately say they have synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 这带来了一个难题，因为艺术家本来就更倾向于不准确地声称自己有联觉。

sentences.en: But there's still more synesthesia among artistic people.
sentences.zh: 但艺术人群中的联觉现象确实更多。

sentences.en: So you have to really use these careful tests.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的必须使用这些严谨的测试。

sentences.en: But yes, you find synesthetes more likely to go into artistic professions and those professions are tied to their synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 但确实，你会发现联觉者更有可能从事艺术职业，并且这些职业与他们的联觉息息相关。

sentences.en: So more musicians with colored music synesthesia, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，拥有彩色音乐联觉的音乐家就更多。

sentences.en: We can also find evidence of higher creativity with lab tests.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以通过实验室测试找到更高创造力的证据。

sentences.en: So, for example, a test of creativity that's quite well known is the remote associates teSt.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个广为人知的创造力测试就是远程联想测验。

sentences.en: And in that test, you're given three words such as...
sentences.zh: 在这个测试中，会给你三个词，比如……

sentences.en: You're given three words and you have to provide the fourth word that links them all.
sentences.zh: 会给你三个词，你必须提供第四个将它们全部联系起来的词。

sentences.en: And I have to think carefully about this so I don't reveal the linking word.
sentences.zh: 我得仔细想想，以免把那个连接词剧透出来。

sentences.en: But an example might be boot...
sentences.zh: 但举个例子，可能是靴子（boot）……

sentences.en: Yeah, this is tough.
sentences.zh: 是的，这挺难的。

sentences.en: Boot, ground, summer.
sentences.zh: 靴子（boot）、地面（ground）、夏天（summer）。

sentences.en: Now, those three words are linked by one other word.
sentences.zh: 现在，这三个词由另一个词联系在一起。

sentences.en: And that other word is camp.
sentences.zh: 那个词就是营地（camp）。

sentences.en: So boot camp, summer camp, campground.
sentences.zh: 所以是新兵训练营（boot camp）、夏令营（summer camp）、露营地（campground）。

sentences.en: And this is a test of creativity and synesthetes perform very well in this teSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个创造力测试，联觉者在这个测试中表现得非常好。

sentences.en: We also have evidence that this creativity is starting quite early.
sentences.zh: 我们还有证据表明，这种创造力在很小的时候就开始显现了。

sentences.en: So we have recently finished a large ERC-funded project.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们最近刚刚完成了一个由欧洲研究理事会（ERC）资助的大型项目。

sentences.en: So European Research Council funded us to look at synesthesia in children for five years.
sentences.zh: 欧洲研究理事会资助我们对儿童的联觉进行了为期五年的研究。

sentences.en: And we can even see those creativity traits emerging early in children.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可以看到这些创造力特征在儿童时期很早就开始萌芽。

sentences.en: So when we find children with synesthesia from the general population, so we're not relying on people to come forward.
sentences.zh: 当我们从普通人群中寻找患有联觉的儿童时，我们不依赖人们主动来找我们。

sentences.en: We've screened thousands of children.
sentences.zh: 我们筛查了成千上万名儿童。

sentences.en: We've found the synesthetes among them.
sentences.zh: 我们在其中找到了联觉者。

sentences.en: And we look at their personality.
sentences.zh: 然后我们观察他们的性格。

sentences.en: And the children don't really realize they're special.
sentences.zh: 孩子们其实并没有意识到自己很特别。

sentences.en: The parents don't know that their children have synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 父母也不知道他们的孩子患有联觉。

sentences.en: But everybody concurs that these synesthetes are higher in the trait of openness to experiences,
sentences.zh: 但所有人都一致认为，这些联觉者在“开放体验”这一性格特质上得分更高，

sentences.en: which is linked to intellectual curiosity, but also creativity.
sentences.zh: 这与求知欲以及创造力息息相关。

sentences.en: So children themselves feel that they're more creative in their personalities.
sentences.zh: 因此，孩子们自己觉得他们的个性更具创造力。

sentences.en: Their parents feel they have more creative personalities.
sentences.zh: 他们的父母也觉得他们拥有更具创造力的个性。

sentences.en: And we can see this from really a young age, from the age of around, I think the children we tested were between six and 10.
sentences.zh: 我们从很小的时候就能看到这一点，从大约……我想我们测试的儿童年龄在六岁到十岁之间。

sentences.en: And we can see these effects emerging, you know, by, if not by six, then by, you know, seven or eight.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到这些效应开始显现，如果不是在六岁时，那也是在七、八岁时。

sentences.en: So yes, creative population.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，他们是富有创造力的人群。

sentences.en: So you've done research that's found that even though most people do not have synesthesia, they do have cross-sensory experiences or associations, for example,
sentences.zh: 那么，你做过的一项研究发现，尽管大多数人没有联觉，但他们确实有跨感官的体验或联想，例如，

sentences.en: associating higher-pitched tones with brighter colors.
sentences.zh: 将较高音调的音符与更明亮的颜色联系起来。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that research and how it relates to synesthesia?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们讲讲那项研究以及它与联觉的关系吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: This is always an area of research that can really play with my head because we look at many different sensory domains and we look at how they cross over in many different ways.
sentences.zh: 这总是一个能让我脑洞大开的研究领域，因为我们观察了许多不同的感官领域，并研究它们如何在许多不同的方式中产生交织。

sentences.en: So I'm going to think carefully.
sentences.zh: 所以我要仔细想想。

sentences.en: So the one that you just described is actually a great finding by, among other people, my colleague, JB Ward.
sentences.zh: 你刚才描述的那项研究，实际上包括我的同事杰米·沃德（JB Ward）在内的多位研究人员得出的极佳发现。

sentences.en: He has shown that people systematically associate the pitch of music with colors in several ways.
sentences.zh: 他已经证明，人们在几种方面会系统性地将音乐的音高与颜色联系起来。

sentences.en: So, for example, higher pitch.
sentences.zh: 例如，更高的音高。

sentences.en: So imagine a test where I play you sounds and I ask you to choose colors and you feel like you're randomly picking because I play you a high-pitched sound,
sentences.zh: 所以想象这样一个测试：我为你播放声音，并要求你选择颜色，你可能会觉得自己是在随机挑选，因为我给你播放高音声音、

sentences.en: a low-pitched sound, you know, a stringed instrument, a piano, and I just ask you to pick colors.
sentences.zh: 低音声音，你知道的，还有弦乐器、钢琴的声音，然后我只是让你去挑选颜色。

sentences.en: And you kind of, you're willing to do this task, although you suspend disbelief because you think you're going to be random.
sentences.zh: 你会有点勉强地完成这个任务，尽管你放下内心的怀疑，因为你觉得自己选的会是随机的。

sentences.en: And actually, people are very, very consistent.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，人们表现出非常非常高的一致性。

sentences.en: And higher pitch sound maps to more luminant colors.
sentences.zh: 更高音调的声音会映射到明度更高的颜色上。

sentences.en: So imagine a piano.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下钢琴。

sentences.en: Imagine I'm on a piano and I'm tinkling on the high notes and I'm crashing on the low notes.
sentences.zh: 想象我在弹钢琴，我在高音区轻轻敲击，在低音区重重弹响。

sentences.en: And I say to you, which one of those is pale yellow?
sentences.zh: 然后我问你，这其中哪一个代表浅黄色？

sentences.en: And you are much more likely to say that the pale yellow is the higher pitch note.
sentences.zh: 你很可能会说，浅黄色代表那个较高的音符。

sentences.en: Okay, and maybe deep dark purple is the low pitch note.
sentences.zh: 好的，也许深沉浓郁的紫色代表低音符。

sentences.en: So there's that association.
sentences.zh: 所以它们之间存在这种关联。

sentences.en: But there are many, many, many of these associations.
sentences.zh: 但这种关联其实有很多很多。

sentences.en: So we have shown that if you give people an identical sweetie, an identical candy, and it either has a rough surface or a smooth surface,
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现，如果你给人们一块完全相同的糖果，而它表面要么粗糙，要么光滑，

sentences.en: they will think that the candy is more sour with the rough surface, even though it has the identical ingredients.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得表面粗糙的糖果更酸，尽管它们的成分完全一样。

sentences.en: So, and here's something quite fun.
sentences.zh: 所以，接下来有个挺有趣的事情。

sentences.en: We have recently been looking at the same phenomenon in dogs.
sentences.zh: 我们最近一直在研究狗身上的这种现象。

sentences.en: So, research in collaboration with my colleague, David Reby, and our student, Anna Korzynovska, who's leading this research,
sentences.zh: 因此，通过与我的同事大卫·雷比（David Reby）以及领导这项研究的学生安娜·科尔济诺夫斯卡（Anna Korzynovska）合作研究，

sentences.en: we have taken domestic dogs into the lab and we show them different objects.
sentences.zh: 我们把家犬带进实验室，向它们展示不同的物体。

sentences.en: So they're either objects of a different size or they're elevated differently in space.
sentences.zh: 这些物体大小不同，或者在空间中的高度不同。

sentences.en: And we play sounds and we train the dogs in advance to go to the object that's making a sound.
sentences.zh: 我们播放声音，并事先训练狗走向发出声音的物体。

sentences.en: And what we find is that they're much more likely to target the small object when the sound is high pitched and the large object when the sound is low pitched.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当声音音调较高时，它们更有可能将目标对准小物体；而当声音音调较低时，则会走向大物体。

sentences.en: And similarly, when the sound is high pitched, they look up to an object up in space.
sentences.zh: 同样，当声音音调高时，它们会抬头看空间中高处的物体。

sentences.en: And when the sound is low pitched, they look down to an object on the ground.
sentences.zh: 当声音音调低时，它们会低头看地面上的物体。

sentences.en: So this shows associations between, on the one hand, sound, and on the other hand, the visual property of size or the visual property of elevation in space.
sentences.zh: 这表明，一方面是声音，另一方面是大小的视觉属性或空间高度的视觉属性，两者之间存在关联。

sentences.en: And that's some really exciting work that's been really fun to conduct.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常令人兴奋的研究工作，开展起来也充满乐趣。

sentences.en: Wow, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 哇，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: So let me change gears a little bit because in addition to synesthesia, you study a variety of other brain and sensory differences.
sentences.zh: 那我稍微换个话题，因为除了共感觉（通感），你还研究了各种其他的大脑和感官差异。

sentences.en: For example, as I said earlier, misophonia, which is an extreme aversion to specific sounds, and aphantasia, which is the inability to picture things in your mind's eye.
sentences.zh: 比如，正如我刚才所说，恐音症（对特定声音极度反感），以及心盲症（无法在脑海中想象事物的画面）。

sentences.en: These seem like really disparate concepts, but how do they tie together?
sentences.zh: 这些看起来是完全不相干的概念，但它们是怎么联系在一起的呢？

sentences.en: That's such a good question because...
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，因为……

sentences.en: Or do they?
sentences.zh: 或者说，它们真的有关联吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a really good question because I found myself working in synesthesia for a couple of decades
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个非常好的问题，因为我研究共感觉已经有几十年了，

sentences.en: and then being introduced to other sensory differences, finding them fascinating,
sentences.zh: 后来接触到其他感官差异，发现它们非常迷人，

sentences.en: berating myself for not having focus, for effectively coming away from synesthesia,
sentences.zh: 我还曾责怪自己不够专心，觉得自己在某种程度上偏离了共感觉的研究，

sentences.en: and then finding out over time that these different conditions are tied by a kind of invisible thread.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，我发现这些不同的状况其实被某种无形的线索串联在了一起。

sentences.en: So all of them are sensory differences, and they all share certain traits in common.
sentences.zh: 所以它们全都是感官差异，并且都有一些共同的特征。

sentences.en: For example, in terms of well-being, so we find that people with these sensory differences,
sentences.zh: 例如，在幸福感方面，我们发现有这些感官差异的人，

sentences.en: even synesthesia that's sometimes considered a gift, can have impairments in their well-being, can have problems in their well-being.
sentences.zh: 即使是常被视为一种天赋的共感觉，其幸福感也可能会受损，在幸福感方面遇到问题。

sentences.en: So for example, in synesthesia, we found that people with synesthesia, with verified synesthesia, are significantly more likely to experience anxiety disorder than other people.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在共感觉方面，我们发现患有共感觉、且经过确诊的人，比其他人明显更有可能经历焦虑症。

sentences.en: We were really surprised about this.
sentences.zh: 对此我们感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: We weren't looking at particularly troubling variants.
sentences.zh: 我们当时并没有特意去研究那些特别令人困扰的变体。

sentences.en: We were looking at coloured letters and numbers, higher rates of anxiety disorder.
sentences.zh: 我们研究的是有颜色的字母和数字，结果却发现焦虑症的发病率更高。

sentences.en: We've just finished a similar study in child synesthetes, and 30% of our child synesthetes under 10 qualify for the category of anxiety disorder, which is really high.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚对儿童共感觉者完成了一项类似的研究，在我们10岁以下的儿童共感觉者中，有30%达到了焦虑症的标准，这个比例非常高。

sentences.en: Usually in children, in our controls, we found it at around less than 10.
sentences.zh: 通常在儿童对照组中，这一比例低于10%。

sentences.en: Synesthetes at 30%.
sentences.zh: 而共感觉者高达30%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And similarly, in these other disciplines, similarly in these other sensory differences.
sentences.zh: 同样，在这些其他学科中，在这些其他感官差异中也是如此。

sentences.en: So misophonia itself is almost defined by difficulties in well-being.
sentences.zh: 因此，恐音症本身几乎就是以幸福感受损为特征的。

sentences.en: So misophonia can give rise to great anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以恐音症会引发巨大的焦虑。

sentences.en: As well as, so misophonia is an extreme hatred of certain sounds.
sentences.zh: 此外，恐音症是对某些声音的极度厌恶。

sentences.en: And those sounds tend to be bodily sounds like coughing or chewing or crunching or swallowing.
sentences.zh: 这些声音往往是身体发出的声音，比如咳嗽、咀嚼、咯吱声或吞咽声。

sentences.en: And it can really give rise to these incredible differences in well-being, anxiety, rage,
sentences.zh: 它确实会给幸福感带来巨大的差异、引发焦虑和愤怒，

sentences.en: uncontrollable feelings, really, that we know are also linked to brain structure.
sentences.zh: 甚至产生真正无法控制的情绪，而我们知道这些也与大脑结构有关。

sentences.en: And what we found in children as young as 10 is that children that we've been able to recognise as having misophonia
sentences.zh: 我们在年仅10岁的儿童身上发现，那些被我们识别出患有恐音症的儿童，

sentences.en: are showing serious differences in their well-being, again, elevated anxiety, as you might expect, but also poorer quality of life, poorer satisfaction in life.
sentences.zh: 其幸福感也出现了严重差异，正如你所料，焦虑情绪加剧，同时生活质量更差，生活满意度也更低。

sentences.en: And then there's also the link with autistic-like traits.
sentences.zh: 此外，它还与类似自闭症的特征有关。

sentences.en: So the more we look at these sensory differences, the more we see parallels with and overlaps with autism.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对这些感官差异研究得越多，就越能看到它们与自闭症的相似之处和重叠之处。

sentences.en: Now, it's not the case that having synesthesia means you're autistic, but it does mean that you're elevated on tests of autism in certain areas.
sentences.zh: 当然，拥有共感觉并不意味着你患有自闭症，但这确实意味着你在某些自闭症测试中的得分更高。

sentences.en: So in misophonia, for example, you're significantly more likely to be diagnosed or recognised as having autism than the average person.
sentences.zh: 例如，患有恐音症的人被诊断或识别为患有自闭症的可能性明显高于普通人。

sentences.en: In synesthesia, you're elevated on the traits of attention to detail.
sentences.zh: 在共感觉方面，你在注重细节的自闭症特征上得分更高。

sentences.en: In synesthesia, you're elevated on the autistic trait of attention to detail.
sentences.zh: 在共感觉方面，你在注重细节的自闭症特征上有所升高。

sentences.en: And in misophonia, no.
sentences.zh: 但在恐音症中则不然。

sentences.en: And in aphantasia, you're elevated in the autistic traits of social difficulties and imagination.
sentences.zh: 而在心盲症中，你在社交困难和想象力这些自闭症特征上的得分更高。

sentences.en: And so, yes, there's this overlap of autistic traits.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，自闭症特征之间存在这种重叠。

sentences.en: There's this overlap in well-being, poorer well-being.
sentences.zh: 幸福感方面也存在这种重叠，即幸福感较差。

sentences.en: So the more I look at many different sensory conditions, the more I'm convinced that they all really fit together
sentences.zh: 因此，我研究的各种感官状况越多，我就越确信它们其实都契合在一起，

sentences.en: in a kind of coherent whole.
sentences.zh: 构成了一个连贯的整体。

sentences.en: Here's one I'll throw at you.
sentences.zh: 我向你抛出这样一个问题。

sentences.en: So we had a guest a few months back, did an episode on face blindness.
sentences.zh: 几个月前我们有一位嘉宾，做了一期关于面孔失认症的节目。

sentences.en: And one of the people is someone I know who has been diagnosed with face blindness.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人是我认识的朋友，她被诊断出患有面孔失认症。

sentences.en: And she recently also learned that she has aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 她最近还得知自己患有心盲症。

sentences.en: Have you looked at those connections?
sentences.zh: 你研究过这些联系吗？

sentences.en: We have.
sentences.zh: 我们研究过。

sentences.en: We have and we are, actually.
sentences.zh: 我们研究过，而且实际上正在研究。

sentences.en: So I think in self-report, people with aphantasia report being poorer at faces, on average.
sentences.zh: 我认为根据自我报告，患有心盲症的人平均而言辨认人脸的能力较差。

sentences.en: And a very nice study we're conducting here at Sussex, led by my PhD student, Carla Dance.
sentences.zh: 我们在萨塞克斯大学正在进行一项非常出色的研究，由我的博士生卡拉·丹斯（Carla Dance）领导。

sentences.en: And in collaboration with my colleague, Graham Hole, who's a witness recognition, a face recognition expert, we've been able to give identikits to people with aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 并且与我的同事格雷厄姆·霍尔（Graham Hole）合作，他是一位目击者辨认、面部识别专家，我们已经能够向心盲症患者提供拼图面部工具包。

sentences.en: And we show them a face and then we ask them to reconstruct the face using these identikits.
sentences.zh: 我们向他们展示一张人脸，然后要求他们用这些拼图工具包重建这张人脸。

sentences.en: And then we give the reconstructed face to a group of controls and ask them, how similar is this reconstructed face with the original?
sentences.zh: 接着，我们将重建的人脸交给一组对照组，问他们：这张重建的人脸与原图有多相似？

sentences.en: And we do that once for our people with aphantasia and once for controls.
sentences.zh: 我们对心盲症患者和对照组分别做了一次这样的测试。

sentences.en: And we're in the middle of doing that study right now.
sentences.zh: 我们目前正在进行这项研究。

sentences.en: And we can see trends in the direction that we'd expect, but we need to finish that study to find out exactly whether it's significant.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到符合预期方向的趋势，但我们需要完成这项研究，才能准确弄清楚它是否具有统计学意义。

sentences.en: But it does look at the moment as if it's trending in the direction of what we would expect, which is poorer face recall for people with aphantasia.
sentences.zh: 但目前看来，它确实朝着我们预期的方向发展，也就是心盲症患者的面部回忆能力较差。

sentences.en: Although I need to add something.
sentences.zh: 尽管我需要补充一点。

sentences.en: This is only a typical of the average aphantasic.
sentences.zh: 这只是平均心盲症患者的典型情况。

sentences.en: So what we actually find is a real spread.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际发现的是一种真正的离散分布。

sentences.en: And it's quite interesting because I have aphantasia myself, but I'm almost a super recognizer.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣，因为我自己就有心盲症，但我几乎是个超级面孔识别者。

sentences.en: So when I perform tests of face recognition, I'm almost good enough to work for the police.
sentences.zh: 所以当我进行面部识别测试时，我的表现好到几乎可以去为警方工作了。

sentences.en: How am I doing that?
sentences.zh: 我是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: How am I doing that?
sentences.zh: 我是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: I have no mental imagery, but I just know very, I'm just able to pick out a face in the crowd very well.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中没有任何视觉意象，但我就是知道很多，我只是非常擅长在人群中挑出一张脸。

sentences.en: So there you go.
sentences.zh: 所以你看。

sentences.en: It's a spread.
sentences.zh: 这是一种分散的情况。

sentences.en: But the average person is less good than controls.
sentences.zh: 但普通人的表现不如对照组。

sentences.en: So I'm just wondering if particularly misophonia and aphantasia are debilitating to the people who have these syndromes.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，尤其是恐音症和心盲症，是否会给患有这些综合症的人带来严重的负面影响？

sentences.en: And is it possible to help someone learn to diminish, say, an aversion to sounds or to teach people how to see things in their mind's eye?
sentences.zh: 是否有可能帮助人们学会减轻对声音的厌恶感，或者教导人们如何在脑海中看到事物？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And I think that is definitely happening a lot more for misophonia.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于恐音症来说，这种情况确实正在变得越来越普遍。

sentences.en: So misophonia is defined as a kind of almost, as an almost chronic condition.
sentences.zh: 所以恐音症几乎被定义为一种慢性疾病。

sentences.en: And misophonia is also really a topic of focus for clinicians.
sentences.zh: 恐音症也是临床医生重点关注的课题。

sentences.en: A lot of clinicians are trying to find out exactly how we can, how we can fix, how we can fix this problem.
sentences.zh: 许多临床医生正试图准确找出我们如何能够、如何能够解决、如何能够解决这个问题的方法。

sentences.en: There are some long-term clinical treatment options.
sentences.zh: 有一些长期的临床治疗选择。

sentences.en: A cognitive behavioral therapy has been tried, a tinnitus retraining therapy, a counter conditioning therapy.
sentences.zh: 人们尝试过认知行为疗法、耳鸣习服疗法以及对抗性条件反射疗法。

sentences.en: They aim to reconceptualize the individual's relationship with sound, or they re-pair unpleasant sounds with more pleasant responses.
sentences.zh: 它们的目的是重新构建个人与声音的关系，或者将不愉快的声音与更愉快的反应重新配对。

sentences.en: Some approaches combine therapy with gentle exposure.
sentences.zh: 一些方法将疗法与温和的暴露疗法结合起来。

sentences.en: It's still quite a young science.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一门很年轻的科学。

sentences.en: It's still quite a young science.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一门很年轻的科学。

sentences.en: There isn't really an outstanding treatment that's emerging above all others.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有出现一种脱颖而出的卓越疗法。

sentences.en: We're just trying, clinicians are just trying different options at the moment, but nothing, some of them are effective, but not across the board.
sentences.zh: 临床医生目前只是在尝试不同的选择，但并没有哪一种能包治百病，尽管其中某些方法确实有效。

sentences.en: Aphantasia is an interesting one.
sentences.zh: 心盲症是一个有趣的例子。

sentences.en: People aren't really trying to improve imagery at the moment in aphantasics.
sentences.zh: 目前大家并没有真正试图去改善心盲症患者的视觉想象力。

sentences.en: I mean, I know personally, I found out I had aphantasia around 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就我个人而言，我大约在10年前发现自己患有心盲症。

sentences.en: I was having an interesting chat with a colleague about synesthetes, and I said to him, these synesthetes are reporting that they can see pictures in their mind's eye.
sentences.zh: 当时我和一位同事在愉快地聊着关于共感觉者的事，我对他说，这些共感觉者报告说他们能在脑海中看到画面。

sentences.en: So if I say pig, they literally see an image of a pig.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我说“猪”，他们真的会看到一头猪的图像。

sentences.en: And I was speaking to my colleague, Bob Blogey, who said, well, that's what everybody does, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我当时在和我的同事鲍勃·布洛吉（Bob Blogey）交谈，他说：“哦，这不就是所有人都会的吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, no, you don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我说：“不，你不明白。”

sentences.en: They see a picture in their mind.
sentences.zh: “他们在脑海里看到了一幅画。”

sentences.en: He said, yeah, that's what everybody does.
sentences.zh: 他说：“对啊，每个人都这样。”

sentences.en: So from that moment, 10 years ago, I have tried, personally speaking, I've tried to construct images.
sentences.zh: 所以从10年前的那一刻起，就我个人而言，我一直试图构建图像。

sentences.en: I don't, I haven't had a great deal of success, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我并没有取得多大的成功。

sentences.en: Although that's an N of one, so who knows?
sentences.zh: 尽管这只是个例（N=1），所以谁知道呢？

sentences.en: So maybe we might try it.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们可能会尝试一下。

sentences.en: But really, the difference between aphantasia and misophonia is that people with aphantasia are getting on fine.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，心盲症和恐音症的区别在于，心盲症患者生活得很好。

sentences.en: They're just getting on fine with their life.
sentences.zh: 他们的生活过得很顺心。

sentences.en: They really have no idea they're different.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道自己有什么不同。

sentences.en: They understand visual imagery as a metaphor.
sentences.zh: 他们把视觉意象理解为一种隐喻。

sentences.en: You know, they, it's really not a big deal in my life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在我的生活中真的不算什么大事。

sentences.en: I'm not very good at interior decorating.
sentences.zh: 我不太擅长室内装修。

sentences.en: I find that quite hard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那挺难的。

sentences.en: What's this sofa going to look like against that wall?
sentences.zh: 这个沙发靠着那堵墙会是什么样子呢？

sentences.en: Really, apart from that, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，真的没什么问题。

sentences.en: Well, this has been just amazingly interesting, Dr. Simna.
sentences.zh: 好吧，西姆娜博士，这次谈话真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: I've really enjoyed talking to you.
sentences.zh: 和你聊天我真的很开心。

sentences.en: I appreciate your, your taking the time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's been, it's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常愉快的经历。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。
